record.paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
record.original_question: For the Blaschke products Q_{a,α}(z)=P_a z^2(z+a)/(1+az), where a>3 and P_a is chosen so that the restriction to the unit circle has rotation number α, suppose α is a Brjuno number. If there is a maximal interval (a0,+∞) on which Q_{a,α} is analytically conjugate to the rigid rotation R_α(z)=e^{2πiα}z, how smooth is the conjugacy at the endpoint a0, and how does that smoothness depend on α?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the family of degree-4 Blaschke products
$$Q_{a,\alpha}(z) = P_a\, z^2 \cdot \frac{z+a}{1+az},$$
where $a \in (3,+\infty)$ is a real parameter and $P_a \in \mathbb{S}^1$ is the unique unimodular constant chosen so that the rotation number of the restriction $Q_{a,\alpha}\!\restriction_{\mathbb{S}^1}$ to the unit circle is equal to a prescribed irrational number $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. Assume that $\alpha$ is a Brjuno number, i.e. $\sum_{n\ge 0} \frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n} < \infty$, where $(p_n/q_n)$ are the convergents of the continued-fraction expansion of $\alpha$.

For each such $\alpha$, suppose that there exists a maximal open interval $(a_0(\alpha), +\infty)$ with $a_0(\alpha) \ge 3$ such that for every $a \in (a_0(\alpha), +\infty)$ the restriction $Q_{a,\alpha}\!\restriction_{\mathbb{S}^1}$ is analytically conjugate to the rigid rotation $R_\alpha(z) = e^{2\pi i \alpha} z$, while $Q_{a_0(\alpha),\alpha}\!\restriction_{\mathbb{S}^1}$ is not analytically conjugate to $R_\alpha$.

Determine the regularity (e.g. $C^k$, $C^\infty$, quasisymmetric, Hölder, etc.) of the conjugacy between $Q_{a_0(\alpha),\alpha}\!\restriction_{\mathbb{S}^1}$ and $R_\alpha$ at the endpoint $a = a_0(\alpha)$, and describe how this regularity depends on the arithmetic properties of $\alpha$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on Herman rings of Blaschke-type families (including surgery results showing real-analytic parametrization by the modulus of the Herman ring for Brjuno rotation numbers, and studies of degenerate Herman rings) does not appear to resolve the endpoint regularity question for the conjugacy at $a_0(\alpha)$. Surveys of Herman-ring open problems continue to list endpoint/boundary behavior questions of this kind, suggesting the precise smoothness at the endpoint and its dependence on $\alpha$ remain open.

status_evidence.title: Surgery on Herman rings of the standard Blaschke family
status_evidence.snippet: Using quasiconformal surgery ... if θ is of Brjuno type, the curve of parameters can be parameterized real analytically by the modulus of the Herman ring, from a=M(θ) up to ∞.
status_evidence.claim: For Brjuno α the parameter curve is real-analytically parametrized by the Herman-ring modulus up to its collapse, but endpoint conjugacy regularity is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Herman Rings: Structure, Dynamics, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems concerning Herman rings and their boundary/degeneration behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Endpoint regularity questions related to the collapse of Herman rings remain among the open problems.

status_evidence.title: Rational maps with smooth degenerate Herman rings
status_evidence.snippet: Degenerate Herman rings that are smooth cannot contain any critical points.
status_evidence.claim: Smoothness of degenerate Herman rings is constrained but the specific endpoint smoothness for the cubic Blaschke family is not determined.
